verdict.rationale: Copilot documents natural-language chat in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio and the terminal, where it can explain concepts, propose edits and validate files in agent mode. Autofix gives contextual explanations and fixes for vulnerabilities, and code review flags issues with severity levels. None of these are explicitly documented as a debugging or troubleshooting workflow. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of debugging via natural-language queries (e.g., explaining errors or stack traces, diagnosing failing tests) and independent hands-on corroboration of debugging quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug issues and troubleshoot using natural-language queries

citations.quote: Copilot in your editor does it all, from explaining concepts and completing code, to proposing edits and validating files with agent mode.
GitHub Copilot Autofix provides contextual explanations and code suggestions to help developers fix vulnerabilities in code
chat functionality is currently available only in Visual Studio Code, JetBrains, and Visual Studio
GitHub Copilot is also supported in terminals through GitHub CLI and as a chat integration in Windows Terminal Canary.
